Title: The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny
Author: Kiran Desai
My Review:
2.5/5
if I hadn't read beyond 75%, I would have given it 3 stars, if I hadn't read beyond 30% I would have probably given it 4 stars. It just progressively linearly fell apart. There is one theme - loneliness, but it just doesn't justify the length and verbosity of this book. Not that I know much about editing technicalities, but I feel a good snipping would have elevated the novel so much. Better yet, if they had partitioned each individual subplot into a short story of its own, I'd read that.
It started out very well, and I was very excited after reading the first few chapters that okay - very relatable, very fresh (I love the delhi references albeit only lodhi gardens and hauz khas) and I could build the world of the story.
But when you want to span and descriptively explain every one of the 10 cities, give a character arc to more than 20 characters and introduce atleast 50 others to "add" to the plot, in the same novel, you do it usually at the expense of tiring out the reader. And I was dead tired.

Title: One of Us Is Lying (One of Us Is Lying, #1)
Author: Karen M. McManus
My Review:
It all started with me on goodreads and watching booktube about the world of new age books. Who does not know about the classics but I wanted to get the feel of books of my time. Especially YA books. Although this book was not a new genre for me but I was a bit taken aback by the depiction of lives of people in this book.
Anyway.

This is a book about 4 people narrated individually by themselves to create the feel that we get into the heads of 4 different people each time. But the author isn't able to accomplish that as it becomes pretty clear with the repetitive use of language and slangs. So even if this was written as the "omniscient narrator" you couldn't have spotted the difference. It would surely have been great if the author tried changing the style with each character.

With that let us observe our characters who were my high school fellows for a week (yeah! I was hooked for a week). I am not going to repeat the descriptions we have at the back of the book yet there is not a better way.
We have Addy who was the high school princess and is in the most popular group in the school.
Cooper, the jock planning to do great in baseball and the most handsome guy in school.
Bronwyn, the topper with a perfect life and family.
Nate, the i-never-cared-and-would-never guy whose family and life are already in turmoil when a guy, Simon chokes to death in a detension with these same people.
Having read so many (I mean so many...check my read shelf) murder mystery books I was expecting something like the ones I have read. This was before I started reading. However over time I understood that this was mainly about the effects of newly arised suspicion, heartbreak, friendship and love on 17 years olds. And I am happy that this book was different and relatable to an extent.
In the end I think it was a good book for a start and hoping to read "One Of Us is Next" soon.
